issues.reason: Manner is defined for adverbs answering 'how' and the instruction set explicitly says to leave an unrepresentable adverbial out rather than mis-slot it into Manner; 'initially' is a sequence adverb, so the atom claims the predicting was done in an 'initially' way, which is false.

(Member sk_sales_1 sale) types an aggregate as one sale and so asserts a single sale worth $6.9-7.5 billion; a plural carrying an aggregate measure is the crates case - GroupOf with the measure on the group.

gaps_confirmed: a magnitude scale word inside a money amount ('$6.9 billion') - no licensed multiplier, so the coined billion_dollar will not compare with plain dollar measures
a non-factive prediction whose content is an NP complement ('predicted sales of between X and Y') - sealing is finite-clause-only, so the predicted range is asserted at top level as fact
a temporal adjunct whose object is a period NP ('at the end of the second quarter') - Time is defined for structured calendar terms and deictic/named constants, not a minted witness
an ordinal naming a calendar/fiscal sub-period ('the second quarter') - Ordinal's scale slot is the associated event or an '-est' dimension, so a cycle like year has no standing there
a two-sided numeric range ('between X and Y') has no named form; the parse composes MeasureAtLeast + MeasureAtMost
new_gaps: a sequence / ordering adverb ('initially', 'originally', 'later') has no licensed slot at all - Manner answers 'how', Time takes calendar terms or deictic constants, and Before needs a second eventuality, so the adverbial has to be dropped
'sales' as an aggregate revenue term - GroupOf forces a count reading (a set of sale events) onto what the text uses as a single money aggregate; there is no mass-aggregate typing
repair_summary: Removed (Manner sk_predict_1 initially) - the sequence adverb has no licensed slot, so it is left out rather than mis-slotted, and the gap is recorded. Retyped the plural as (GroupOf sk_sales_1 sale) so the range measures read as the group aggregate, per the crates precedent.
notes: Gap 2 is the sharpest here: the top-level MeasureAtLeast/AtMost do assert a range the text says only that Intel predicted, but sealing is finite-clause-only and no other carrier is licensed, so it stays a registered limitation rather than a repairable defect. billion_dollar, the Ordinal-on-year and the Time-on-witness improvisations were left untouched - each is true and well-typed inside a gap the reviewer registered.
